newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - January 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - January 15.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Two Dutch policemen, on the trail of Dutch child sex abusers, arrive in Sri Lanka to investigate pornographic centre allegedly run by Dutch nationals.
The Ceylon Tourist Board goes on the Internet.

Indian Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral to visit Sri Lanka next week for joint talks. The visit is the first by a senior minister since Prime Minister Deve Gowda's 13-member coalition government came to power in India last year.

Main opposition United National Party (UNP) should help government get its devolution proposals passed through parliament before it goes to a national referrendum, Tamil intellectuals tell UNP leader Ranil Wickremesinghe.
Air force plane bombs village at Vishwamadu in northern Kilinochchi district, killing three civilians and wounding 13 more, International Red Cross officials say.
Defence Ministry committee on missing people in Jaffna begins sittings on January 18 in Jaffna.
Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) guerrillas attack army's defences at Chettikulam in the northern Vavuniay district. At least one soldier and 15 guerrillas killed.

The UNP is committed to total freedom of the media and supports journalists who will picket in Colombo today against the government's policy of harrassing media personnel in the guise of national security, UNP's general secretary Gamini Athukorala says.
Journalists from the electronic and print media to conduct a 'sathyagraha' in Colombo on Wednesday to demonstrate solidarily against what they say is repressive government media policy.
Working Journalists Association says will not particpate in today's demonstration because it is politically motivated.
